items.text: The Canadian flag was 60 years old on February 15. George F. G. Stanley designed it, and it became a symbol of Canada’s pride and unity . Many Canadians feel happy when they see it because it reminds them of their country’s beauty and freedom. People think of the flag when they watch hockey games or important events. Some say it shows how big and comfortable Canada is. Others believe it became even more important in recent years because of world events. Experts say the Canadian flag is simple and easy to remember. Newcomers to Canada love it because they feel safe and welcome here. Many people are happy to live in a country that gives them a good life. Difficult words: pride (feeling pleased because you or somebody else did something good), unity (being together as one), newcomer (a person who is new to a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Canadian flag is 60 years old on February 15. It is red and white with a big maple leaf. Many people love the flag. It shows Canada’s pride . Canadians feel happy when they see the flag at hockey games or special days. It also makes them think of Canada’s big land and free life. Some people say that the flag is even more special now because of problems in the world. Flag experts say that it is a great flag. It is easy to see and know. Many people know the flag. People who move to Canada like the flag, too. It means freedom and a good life. Many Canadians feel lucky to live in this country. Difficult words: maple (a tree with colorful leaves in the autumn), pride (a happy feeling about something good you do), freedom (being free). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Universal Studios Singapore has just opened Minion Land, an exciting new section based on Despicable Me. The area includes three zones: Minion Marketplace, Gru’s Neighborhood, and Super Silly Fun Land. Minion Marketplace offers shops filled with Minion-themed clothing, toys, and souvenirs. Visitors will find items like Minion goggles and plushies , as well as a store with stylish apparel . Gru’s Neighborhood is home to Despicable Me Minion Mayhem, a motion- simulator ride that lets visitors experience what it is like to be a Minion. The ride takes place inside Gru’s house, where guests can see objects from the movies before enjoying an adventure filled with drops and water effects. Super Silly Fun Land has carnival-style games, including one where players launch bananas into baskets. There are also rides and a restaurant that serves Minion-inspired food, such as Stuart’s Japanese Curry Karaage. Visitors will be able to take pictures with life-sized Minion statues and spot hidden references to the movies. Difficult words: plushy (a soft stuffed toy), apparel (clothing), simulator (a machine on which people can practice operating a vehicle or experience a real-life situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Minion Land is now open at Universal Studios Singapore. This new area has three parts: Minion Marketplace, Gru’s Neighborhood, and Super Silly Fun Land. Minion Marketplace has different shops where visitors can buy Minion clothes, toys, and other fun things. One shop sells cool Minion-style fashion, while another has plush toys and gifts. Gru’s Neighborhood has a special ride called Minion Mayhem. People sit in a moving seat and feel like they are flying through Gru’s house. The ride has exciting drops and water splashes. Super Silly Fun Land has games and rides. One game lets players throw bananas into baskets. There is also a restaurant with food like Minion-shaped rice and banana popcorn. Visitors can take pictures with big Minion statues and look for small surprises from the movies. Difficult words: plush (soft and fluffy), exciting (fun and full of action). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Minion Land is a new place at Universal Studios Singapore. It has shops, games, rides , and a restaurant. In Minion Marketplace, people can buy Minion toys, clothes, and bags. Some toys are soft and small. Gru’s Neighborhood has a fun ride called Minion Mayhem. The ride moves fast. People feel like they are flying. There are big drops and water splashes . Super Silly Fun Land has rides and games. In one game, people throw bananas into a basket. There is also a place to eat. People can try Minion-shaped rice and banana popcorn. Visitors can take photos with big Minion statues. There are also small fun things from the Minion movies. Difficult words: ride (a machine which moves people for fun), drop (falling), splash (when water or other liquid falls onto something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At the Munich Security Conference, US Vice President JD Vance claimed that free speech is in retreat in Europe and that European voters never chose to ‘open the floodgates’ to migrants. He also argued that limits on freedom of expression pose a greater threat to democracy than Russian military aggression. His speech, delivered in a firm tone, surprised many European leaders, particularly in Germany. According to DW’s Chief International Editor Richard Walker, Vance’s remarks were payback for European criticism of the MAGA movement. Some saw his words as an endorsement of far-right parties in Europe, as he criticized the practice of excluding them from coalition governments. German leaders, including Defense Minister Boris Pistorius, strongly rejected his comments, calling them unacceptable. Observers noted that Vance’s speech may deepen tensions between the US and Europe, particularly as it comes just before key elections in Germany. While some people ignored his statements, others think they show growing transatlantic political disagreements. Difficult words: retreat (moving back or becoming weaker), payback (the act of taking revenge), endorsement (support). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

At the Munich Security Conference, US Vice President JD Vance said free speech in Europe is under threat . He also said that European voters never wanted large numbers of migrants to enter their countries. His speech shocked many European leaders, especially in Germany. Vance argued that stopping free speech is more dangerous for democracy than Russian military actions. Some believe his words were a response to European criticism of the MAGA movement. He also seemed to support far-right parties in Europe, saying governments should not exclude them. German leaders strongly disagreed with him. Vence’s speech may create more problems between the US and Europe, especially before Germany’s elections. Some people ignored his comments, but others think they show growing disagreements between Europe and the US. Difficult words: threat (danger), response (an answer), exclude (not to be part of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At a big meeting in Germany, US Vice President JD Vance says that free speech in Europe is in danger . He also said that people in Europe do not want migrants to come. His words surprise and upset many European leaders. Vance says that stopping free speech is worse than war. Some people think he says it because of criticism of the MAGA movement. He also says that far-right parties in Europe should be in governments. German leaders do not like his words at all. What Vence says may cause problems between the US and Europe. Some people do not care. Others think that more problems will come soon. Difficult words: free speech (when you can openly say what you think), danger (a situation when something bad could happen), criticism (saying that something or someone is bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists are closely tracking asteroid 2024 YR4, which was discovered last year. It is estimated to be between 40 and 90 meters wide and may come very close to Earth on December 22, 2032. Currently, there is a 2% chance that it could hit the planet, which is slightly higher than previous predictions. However, experts stress there is still a 98% probability that it won’t collide with Earth. When an asteroid is first spotted, there is a large area of uncertainty regarding its exact path. As more data is gathered, scientists can refine their calculations and often rule out a collision. If further observations confirm that the asteroid is on a direct course for Earth, a deflection mission could be launched. NASA has already tested this approach by successfully altering the orbit of another asteroid. For now, astronomers will continue to observe 2024 YR4, using tools like the James Webb Space Telescope, before it moves out of sight until 2028. Difficult words: refine (to improve), rule out (to state that something is impossible or will not happen), deflection (changing direction). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last year, scientists found an asteroid 2024 YR4, which they are watching because it may hit Earth. The asteroid is between 40 and 90 meters wide and may come close to Earth on December 22, 2032. There is a small chance, about 2%, that it could hit our planet. Scientists say there is no reason to worry because the chance of it missing Earth is still very high. When astronomers spot an asteroid, they don’t know exactly where it will go. As they collect more information, they can calculate its path better. If they see that it is coming towards Earth, they can try to change its direction . NASA tested this method by hitting an asteroid with a spacecraft. For now, scientists will keep studying 2024 YR4 before it becomes i nvisible in May, and they won’t see it again until 2028. Difficult words: path (a track between one place and another), direction (the way something is moving), invisible (not possible to see). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists find an asteroid called 2024 YR4. It is big, between 40 and 90 meters wide . It may come close to Earth on December 22, 2032. The chance of it hitting Earth is small, only 2%. Scientists say that we should not worry. The asteroid will probably miss our planet. At first, scientists are not sure where an asteroid will go. Later, they get more information. They can see its way better. If it comes toward Earth, they can try to push it away. NASA already tries this before. Scientists will keep watching the asteroid before it moves away in May. After that, they will not see it again until 2028. Difficult words: asteroid (a big rock in space), wide (how large something is from one side to the other), hit (to crash into something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Santorini has been targeted by fake viral videos falsely showing a volcanic eruption. Some videos are AI-generated, while others are miscaptioned . They have gained thousands of views on TikTok and X, misleading many people. One video shows lava flowing into the sea, but experts identified signs of AI, such as unnatural water movement. Another video of people running in fear has distorted figures, proving it was AI-made. A third video, showing an island with smoke, is not AI-generated but is actually from New Zealand’s White Island eruption in 2019. Rumors claim Turkey is behind the misinformation. Allegedly Turkey wants to hurt Santorini’s tourism, but there is no evidence. Meanwhile, Santorini is experiencing a real crisis, with over 800 earthquakes since January. Experts say the tremors are not linked to the island’s volcano, but the risk of a stronger earthquake remains uncertain. A state of emergency is in place until March, and thousands have left the island. The Greek Prime Minister announced 3 million euros for an emergency evacuation route. Difficult words: miscaptioned (provided with a wrong piece of text under a picture or video), distorted (changed unnaturally), tremor (a small earthquake). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People share fake videos of a volcano eruption in Santorini on TikTok and X. AI makes some videos, while other videos are real, but there is wrong information. They confused many people. One video shows lava in the sea, but experts noticed strange details, like unrealistic water. Another video of people running looks fake because their faces are blurred . A third video shows real smoke, but it is actually from New Zealand’s 2019 eruption. Some people believe Turkey made these videos to hurt Santorini’s tourism. Santorini is having real problems. Since January, more than 800 small earthquakes hit the island, and many people left. No one knows if a bigger earthquake will happen. The Greek government is giving 3 million euros for help. Difficult words: confused (unable to think clearly), unrealistic (not looking as things are), blurred (not clear). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Fake videos of a volcano eruption in Santorini are spreading online. AI makes some of them, and others are not real videos of Santorini. Many people believe them, but they are false. One video shows lava in the sea. But the water looks strange . Another shows people running, but their faces look wrong. A third video is from New Zealand, not Santorini. Some people think that Turkey makes the videos. They believe that Turkey wants to hurt Santorini’s tourism. But Santorini has a real problem—many small earthquakes . Over 800 earthquakes happen since January. Many people leave the island. The Greek government is giving 3 million euros to help people leave safely . Experts do not know if a big earthquake will come. Difficult words: strange (not usual), earthquake (when the earth moves), safely (without danger). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

African cuisine is gaining popularity in London, with restaurants like Akoko leading the way. Akoko is one of the few African restaurants with a Michelin star, offering a fine dining experience that blends West African ingredients with modern techniques. Founder Aji Akokomi was inspired to create Akoko after noticing a lack of African restaurants that matched the quality of other fine dining establishments. He wanted to introduce exceptional West African cuisine to London in a sophisticated way. Akoko is part of a larger trend, with restaurants like Chisuru also attracting attention for their creative approach to African flavors. Many Londoners, including those from African backgrounds, appreciate the recognition of traditional ingredients in high-end restaurants. Aji believes that African fine dining will continue to grow in London. The increasing number of West African restaurants and their success suggests that African cuisine is becoming a key part of the city’s diverse food scene, from Michelin-starred dining to street food markets. Difficult words: fine dining (a restaurant experience that is more special and expensive than at a typical restaurant), sophisticated (of high quality and style), high-end (higher in price and of better quality than most others). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

African food is becoming more popular in London, and Akoko is one of the most famous African restaurants. It has a Michelin star and mixes West African ingredients with modern cooking styles. The owner, Aji Akokomi, wanted to create a fine-dining African restaurant because he couldn’t find one that had the quality of French or Chinese restaurants. He wanted Akoko to serve high-quality African food in a stylish way. Other restaurants, like Chisuru, are also helping African food grow in London. People from African countries feel at home with flavors they know, while others enjoy trying something new. Aji believes that African fine dining will continue to grow. With more West African restaurants opening, African food is becoming an important part of London’s restaurant scene . Difficult words: fine dining (a special and expensive style of eating at a restaurant), stylish (of good quality and design), scene (an area of activity or interest). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

African food is becoming popular in London. One restaurant, Akoko, has a Michelin star. It mixes West African ingredients with modern cooking. Aji Akokomi has the restaurant. He wants to create a fine-dining African restaurant. He cannot find one in London, so he makes Akoko. He can share high-quality African food here. Other restaurants, like Chisuru, are also helping African food grow. People from Africa feel happy to see their food in top restaurants. Others love trying new flavors. Aji thinks that African food will keep growing. More West African restaurants are opening, and African food is becoming an important part of London. Difficult words: popular (when many people like someone or something), ingredient (one of more parts of a meal), fine dining (a special and expensive style of eating). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The UK and the US didn’t sign an international AI agreement at a global summit in Paris. The declaration , supported by 60 countries including France, China, and India, promotes an open, inclusive, and ethical approach to AI. The UK government stated it couldn’t agree with all parts of the declaration and would only support initiatives that align with national interests. The summit focused on reducing the digital gap, ensuring AI safety, and making the technology more transparent . India’s Prime Minister, Narendra Modi, emphasized the need for global efforts to regulate AI while recognizing its potential to create jobs. He highlighted India’s focus on AI development and innovation, despite concerns about risks such as misinformation and job losses. Meanwhile, US Vice President J.D. Vance encouraged Europe to embrace AI optimistically. He stressed the importance of international cooperation while ensuring that the US remains a leader in AI. The discussion about AI’s risks and opportunities will continue at the next summit in India. Difficult words: declaration (an official statement), transparent (open and honest), embrace (to accept or welcome). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The UK and the US didn’t sign an AI agreement at a global summit in Paris. Many countries, like France, China, and India, agreed to make AI development open, fair, and safe. The UK said it didn’t agree with everything in the document and would only support what is best for the country. The meeting focused on making AI safe and easy to use for everyone. India’s Prime Minister, Narendra Modi, said AI is growing fast and can create jobs. He also warned about risks like fake news. The US Vice President, J.D. Vance, said Europe should be more positive about AI. He wants countries to work together and take the US as a leader in AI. The next AI meeting will be in India. Difficult words: global summit (a meeting of world leaders or other important people), development (how things grow or change over time), positive (seeing the good in something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A big meeting on AI takes place in Paris, France. The UK and the US do not sign an AI agreement . Other countries, like France, China, and India, say that AI must be open, fair, and safe. The UK does not agree with everything. It will only sign what is good for the country. India’s leader says that AI is growing fast. AI can create new jobs. But it also has risks , like fake news. The US leader says that AI is good. People should not be afraid of it. He wants countries to work together. But the US must be number one in AI. The next AI meeting will be in India. Difficult words: sign (to write a name on a letter, card, or document), agreement (a deal), risk (a possible danger). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

CBC reporter Sandra Abma took part in a cold-water plunge in Ottawa’s Rideau River, where she met enthusiasts who believe in its benefits. Richard Lee, a member of Coldplay Ottawa, has been practicing ice plunges daily for four years. He first tried it after suffering from a traumatic hockey injury that caused depression, anxiety, and brain fog. He claims that after just two minutes in freezing water, he felt mentally stronger. Professor François Hammond has studied the effects of extreme cold on the human body for 25 years, including its use in military training. While many believe in the health benefits of cold plunging, he warns that scientific proof is still lacking. Some early studies suggest it may help with chronic pain, but more research is needed. Before plunging, Lee guided Abma through warm-up exercises and safety precautions. Although shocked by the cold, she completed the challenge and found the experience exhilarating . Difficult words: plunge (jump or dive quickly and energetically), traumatic (very upsetting or causing serious injury), exhilarating (making someone feel very excited and full of energy). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

CBC reporter Sandra Abma tried cold-water swimming in Ottawa’s Rideau River. Richard Lee, a member of a local cold- plunge group, started ice bathing four years ago. After a serious hockey injury, he had depression and trouble thinking clearly. He says that after staying in the cold water for two minutes, he felt much better. Professor François Hammond started studying the effects of cold on the body 25 years ago. Some people say ice baths help with health problems, but science has no evidence yet. Some early studies show it might help with pain, but there must be more research. Before going into the water, Lee showed Abma warm-up exercises and safety steps. She found the water freezing but finished the challenge successfully. Difficult words: plunge (to jump quickly), effect (a change which is a result of something), evidence (anything that helps to prove that something is or is not true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

CBC reporter Sandra Abma goes into cold water in Ottawa’s Rideau River. Richard Lee does ice swimming often. He helps her. He starts four years ago after a bad hockey accident. He feels sad and has trouble thinking. After two minutes in the cold water, he feels much better. Professor François Hammond studies how cold water affects the body. Some people say that ice swimming is good for health. But scientists are not sure yet. Some studies say it may help with pain . Before jumping in, Abma does warm-up exercises. The water is very cold, but she does it and feels happy. Difficult words: affect (to make something or someone change), pain (when a part of your body hurts), warm-up (a short exercise which prepares you for a sport or activity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Rose prices are at a record high, and tariffs could make them even more expensive. However, there are still affordable Valentine’s Day gifts available. Some cost as little as 5 dollars, making it easy to celebrate without spending too much. Walmart offers gifts under 10 dollars, including teddy bears, chocolates, and long-stem roses made from fabric. Chocolate remains one of the most popular Valentine’s Day gifts. Some stores sell small boxes for around 5 dollars. Retail experts suggest other budget-friendly ideas, such as stylish accessories, personalized tumblers , kitchen tools, and beauty products. A gift card to a favorite store is also a good choice. To save money, it is best to shop before prices go up. Comparing prices and using coupons can also help. Some people prefer giving thoughtful, personal gifts instead of expensive ones. One shopper, for example, bought a small gift for her mother before flying to visit her in person. Difficult words: retail (selling goods to the public, usually in shops), tumbler (a drinking glass with straight sides and no handle), coupon (discount offer that lowers prices). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Roses are very expensive this year, and prices may go even higher. But there are still many cheap Valentine’s Day gifts. You can find gifts for as little as 5 dollars. Walmart sells gifts under 10 dollars, like teddy bears, chocolates, and fake roses. Chocolate is always a favorite gift. Some small boxes cost about 5 dollars. Experts say other good ideas are stylish accessories , tumblers with names, kitchen tools, or beauty products. A gift card to a favorite store is also a nice present. To save money, buy gifts early before prices go up. You can also compare prices in different shops. Some people like giving small but special gifts. One shopper bought a gift for her mother before flying to see her. Difficult words: stylish (fashionable and attractive), accessory (a small thing like jewelry or a bag), tumbler (a drinking glass). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Roses cost a lot of money this year. But you can still buy cheap gifts for Valentine’s Day. Some gifts cost only 5 dollars. Walmart sells small teddy bears, chocolates, and fake roses for under 10 dollars. Chocolate is always a good gift. Some small chocolate boxes cost about 5 dollars. Other good gifts are bags, cups with names, cooking tools, or beauty products. A gift card to a favorite shop is also a nice idea. To save money, buy gifts early. Some people like small gifts that are special . One woman buys a gift for her mom before flying to see her. Difficult words: fake (not real), beauty (things which make you look nicer, like makeup), special (different in a good way). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Imane Khelif and Caster Semenya have faced controversy regarding their eligibility to compete as women in elite sports. The issue is linked to intersex variations, also called differences in sex development (DSD). These conditions mean a person’s biological characteristics don’t fit typical male or female patterns. While most variations don’t provide an advantage in sports, some cases raise concerns due to factors like high testosterone levels. In the past, sports organizations used chromosome tests to determine sex, but these were later abandoned. Today, rules differ across sports federations. World Athletics requires athletes with certain conditions to lower their testosterone levels, while the International Olympic Committee focuses on inclusion and doesn’t enforce strict eligibility rules. Semenya, who has XY chromosomes and internal testes, was banned from competing in certain events unless she reduced her testosterone. She fought against these rules, arguing that they were unfair and discriminatory . The debate continues, with scientists and sports officials divided on the issue. Difficult words: eligibility (the right to do something), differ (to be different or dissimilar), discriminatory (treating people unfairly). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Athletes Imane Khelif and Caster Semenya have a condition called DSD, which means their bodies are different from typical male or female bodies. Some people believe this gives them an unfair advantage because they have higher testosterone levels. In the past, sports organizations tested athletes’ chromosomes to decide if they could compete as women. Today, different organizations have different rules. World Athletics says some athletes must lower their testosterone, but the International Olympic Committee doesn’t have strict rules and focuses on inclusion . Semenya was born and raised as a woman. She couldn’t compete unless she changed her natural hormone levels. She fought against this rule, which she found unfair. The argument about fairness in women’s sports is still going on. Difficult words: advantage (something that helps someone do better), inclusion (including all people and groups in activities or organizations), argument (a reason which supports an idea or action). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Imane Khelif and Caster Semenya are athletes who want to compete as women. But some people say that they have an unfair advantage . Their bodies are different. They do not look like other women. They have a condition called DSD. Some women with DSD have more testosterone. Testosterone makes their bodies bigger and stronger. Before, sports organizations use tests to check if athletes were women. Now, different groups have different rules. Some say that women with high testosterone must lower it. Others say that they don’t need to. Semenya cannot compete. She must change testosterone in her body. She thinks it is unfair. People have different views on this. It is difficult to be fair in women’s sports these days. Difficult words: compete (to try to be better than others), advantage (something that helps someone do better), condition (the state of things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Baltic states – Latvia, Estonia, and Lithuania – have officially joined the European electricity system after disconnecting from Russia. This change is important because they had depended on Russian electricity for decades. The process took years, involving the construction of new power lines to connect them with Finland, Sweden, and Poland. It also had strong political meaning, as relations between these countries and Russia have been tense since they became independent in the 1990s. On Saturday, the final transmission lines linking them to Russia and Belarus were switched off, and a ceremony was held on Sunday to celebrate the connection to the EU grid . European leaders, including Ursula von der Leyen, attended the event. The Baltic states had informed Russia and Belarus about their plans in 2024 to prevent any conflicts. The move increased their energy security and independence, especially after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. Difficult words: transmission (the act of sending electricity, signals, or messages from one place to another), grid (a network of lines that carry electricity). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Latvia, Estonia, and Lithuania now get electricity from the European system instead of Russia. They used Russian electricity for many years, but now they are connected to Finland, Sweden, and Poland. This change is important because it helps them be safer and more independent . On Saturday, they turned off the last power lines to Russia and Belarus. The next day, they had a ceremony with leaders from Europe, including Ursula von der Leyen. In 2024, the three countries told Russia and Belarus about their plans so there wouldn’t be any problems. Relations with Russia worsened in 2022 because of the war in Ukraine. The Baltic countries want to be part of Europe and not depend on Russia anymore. Difficult words: independent (not needing help or control from others), ceremony (a special event to celebrate something), worsen (to make or become worse). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Latvia, Estonia, and Lithuania now get electricity from Europe, not Russia. Before, they use Russian electricity for a long time. These countries do not want to use Russian electricity anymore. They want to be with Europe. They also feel safer now because they do not need Russia for power. Now, they have new power lines from Finland, Sweden, and Poland. On Saturday, they stop using Russian electricity. On Sunday, they have a big party. Many important people came, like Ursula von der Leyen. In 2024, they tell Russia and Belarus about this change. They do not want any problems with Russia. Difficult words: electricity (power which makes lights and machines work), power line (a cable which carries electricity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Luis Rubiales, the former president of Spain’s football federation, is on trial for sexual assault after kissing player Jenni Hermoso during the 2023 Women’s World Cup celebrations. While Rubiales claims the kiss was consensual , Hermoso has stated otherwise. He also faces a coercion charge for allegedly pressuring her to say she agreed to the kiss. Three of his former colleagues, including the team’s coach, are also on trial for coercion. At first, Rubiales refused to step down, calling the accusations a witch-hunt , but later resigned. If found guilty, he could face a prison sentence. This case has highlighted ongoing sexism in football, despite progress in women’s sports. For many, this trial represents a turning point in Spanish football. Hermoso’s supporters see it as an opportunity to challenge gender inequality in sports and society. The court proceedings have begun in Madrid and will continue until February 19. Difficult words: consensual (agreed by both people), coercion (forcing someone to do something), witch-hunt (a campaign directed against a person or group), sexism (the belief that the members of one sex are less able, skillful, or intelligent). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Luis Rubiales, Spain’s former football president, is on trial for kissing player Jenni Hermoso after the 2023 Women’s World Cup final. He says that Hermoso agreed with the kiss, but she disagrees with that. She also says that Rubiales pressured her to say she accepted the kiss. Three others, including the team’s coach, face similar charges. At first, Rubiales didn’t want to quit his job. He said that it was fake feminism . Later, he quit, and the trial started. Rubiales may even go to prison. This case shows how much sexism there is in football. Many people believe it is an important moment for women in sports. The trial started in Madrid and will continue until February 19. Difficult words: disagree (to not agree), pressure (to try to make someone do or say something), feminism (the idea that women can do and have the same things as men), sexism (unfair treatment because of gender). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Luis Rubiales is an ex-football leader in Spain. He is in trouble because he kisses player Jenni Hermoso at the 2023 Women’s World Cup. Rubiales says that Hermoso agrees with the kiss. But she says no. She says that Rubiales is trying to make her say it is okay. At first, Rubiales does not want to leave his job. He says that people are not fair to him. But later, he leaves his job. And how he may even go to jail. Many people think this case is important for women in sports. They want football to be fair for everyone. The trial starts in Madrid. It will end on February 19. Difficult words: agree (to say yes), case (an example of something happening, one special situation), trial (a legal court case). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

El Salvador has offered to house dangerous criminals deported from the US, including gang members from groups like MS-13 and Tren de Aragua. This announcement came after a meeting between US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele. On his first overseas tour, Rubio is looking to strengthen regional support for the Trump administration’s deportation policies. In addition to accepting its own deported citizens, El Salvador has proposed acting as a third country that takes in criminals from other nations unwilling to accept them, such as Venezuela and Cuba. Bukele even suggested housing dangerous criminals who are US citizens or legal residents, though it is unclear whether the US will consider this offer. While this proposal aligns with the US goal of deporting more criminals, concerns remain over El Salvador’s harsh prison conditions. The agreement details are still being finalized. Difficult words: deportation (forcing someone to leave a country), unwilling (not wanting to do something), align (to match or support an idea or plan). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

El Salvador offered to take in dangerous criminals deported from the US, including gang members. This news came after a meeting between US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele. Rubio is working to get support for Trump’s deportation plans. El Salvador is already accepting its own deported citizens but now wants to take criminals from other countries, such as Venezuela and Cuba, which don’t want them. Bukele also said his country could take dangerous US citizens, but it is unclear if the US will agree. Some people worry about El Salvador’s prisons. More details of the plan will come soon. Difficult words: deported (sent back to another country), deportation (sending someone back to another country), citizen (a person who lives in a particular place or country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The war in Ukraine has raised concerns about nuclear safety, especially at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, which has been caught in the fighting. Rafael Grossi, the head of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), will travel to Moscow to discuss Russia’s continuous attacks on Ukraine’s energy system, which could threaten nuclear facilities. Grossi has maintained communication with Kyiv and Moscow, meeting key figures, including Russian President Vladimir Putin. He noted that the Zaporizhzhia plant, under Russian control, has faced dangerous situations several times. However, he refrained from blaming either side, as the plant is near the front line. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned Russia for attacking energy infrastructure and detaining Ukrainian engineers. Russia’s strikes on power stations risk cutting electricity to nuclear plants, which rely on stable power for cooling systems. If power is lost, emergency diesel generators are the last safeguard against disaster. Difficult words: refrain (to stop oneself from doing something), condemn (to criticize someone or something strongly), safeguard (a person or thing that ensures protection against danger or damage). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Protesters in Nigeria oppose the government’s plan to restart oil production in Ogoniland, one of the most polluted regions in the world. For decades, oil spills have poisoned Ogoniland’s water and land, making life difficult for its people. A 1 billion dollar cleanup project launched in 2018 has failed, leaving residents frustrated and demanding more effort and compensation . Despite the massive budget, cleanup efforts remain ineffective. Many had hoped oil production would bring prosperity, but instead, they lost their clean environment. The cleanup agency HYPREP faces serious allegations of mismanagement . Its leader denies corruption, but Nigerian authorities have warned he could face arrest. As the government moves to restart oil extraction, many fear a repeat of past environmental destruction. Families of activists who lost their lives opposing oil exploitation in 1995 believe their struggle was in vain . For many in Ogoniland, suffering has replaced the prosperity they once expected. Difficult words: compensation (money paid to someone in exchange for something that has been lost or for some problem), mismanagement (managing something badly or wrongly), in vain (without success or a result), exploitation (making use of and benefiting from resources). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: restart (to start again), pollution (dirty water, air, or land), cleanup (putting dirt or pollution away), compensation (money someone gets because of something bad they went through). Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau announced that Canada will impose 25% tariffs on billions of dollars worth of US goods. This decision responds to US President Donald Trump’s tariffs on Canadian and Mexican imports. While Trudeau hoped to negotiate before tariffs take effect on Tuesday, Trump has ignored his calls. Trump has signed an order to apply 25% tariffs on Canadian and Mexican goods and 10% on Chinese imports. He justified these tariffs by blaming both countries for illegal immigration and drug trafficking into the US. Mexico also plans to impose tariffs on US products. President Claudia Sheinbaum rejected US accusations of drug cartel connections and criticized the lack of US action on fentanyl use. Canada’s counter-tariffs target products from Republican-leaning states, such as bourbon from Kentucky and orange juice from Florida. Some provinces are doubling tolls on American trucks and removing US products from store shelves. Economic experts warn that these tariffs could disrupt industries and trigger a recession. Difficult words: tariff (a tax on imported goods), justify (to give a reason for something), disrupt (cause problems). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A medical transport plane crashed near a shopping center in Philadelphia, killing all six people on board, including a child. A person in a car also lost their life, bringing the death toll to seven. Additionally, 19 people were injured and are being treated in hospitals. Investigators, including the FBI, are examining the debris to determine the cause of the crash. The accident was caught on security cameras, showing a fireball engulfing cars and houses. The young girl on board was returning to Mexico after medical treatment. Her mother, two pilots, a doctor, and a paramedic also died. Authorities have warned the public about scams asking for donations related to the crash, stating that no official fundraising efforts have been launched. This incident occurred just two days after another major plane crash in the US, raising concerns about aviation safety. Officials have reassured the public that flying remains safe, but investigations into both accidents continue. Difficult words: death toll (the number of deaths resulting from a particular cause), fireball (a large ball of fire caused by an explosion), scam (a trick). South Sudan has lifted its ban on Facebook and TikTok, which was imposed last week after videos allegedly showing the killings of South Sudanese nationals in Sudan went viral. These videos sparked protests and violence throughout South Sudan. The National Communications Authority confirmed that the disturbing content has been removed from the platforms. The director of the National Communications Authority emphasized that the violence caused by social media highlights the importance of regulating online content while protecting citizens’ rights. Rights groups have accused the Sudanese army of carrying out ethnically-targeted attacks in El Gezira state following the army’s capture of the state capital, Wad Madani. The army, however, described the incidents as individual violations . These attacks, filmed and widely shared, contributed to the unrest . South Sudan has now restored access to the platforms but continues to deal with the fallout of the violence fueled by the videos. Difficult words: violation (breaking a law or agreement), unrest (disorder or trouble in society), fallout (the unpleasant results or effects of an action or event). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Better Dairy, a UK startup, is developing animal-free cheese and yogurt alternatives that aim to be healthier for consumers and better for the environment compared to traditional dairy products. Their goal is to create products that taste, melt, and stretch like regular cheese without involving cows. The company focuses on using precision fermentation to produce milk proteins, such as casein, that are essential for the texture and flavor of cheese. This process avoids the need for cows, reducing the environmental impact of dairy production. Traditional dairy farming produces methane, a harmful greenhouse gas, and uses large amounts of resources like land and water. Better Dairy is producing casein and another protein, osteopontin, at a small scale. However, they plan to increase production and are working on gaining regulatory approval in key markets, including the US. They hope to receive approval for casein by 2028 and osteopontin by 2027, which would mark a significant step in sustainable dairy alternatives. Difficult words: precision (exact or accurate), fermentation (the process of changing food using microorganisms), regulatory (relating to the control of an activity by a set of rules or laws). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Consumer Electronics Show (CES) in Las Vegas showcased the latest health technology, focusing on prevention and data integration. Many devices, such as Withings’ health tracking system, collect personal health information and use artificial intelligence to analyze it. This data can help users understand their health better and even share insights with doctors. A hormone-measuring device allows users to track cortisol and progesterone levels through saliva testing. Over time, users will recognize patterns in their hormone levels, helping them make informed lifestyle decisions. Other innovations included non-invasive glucose monitors, smart rings, and advanced blood pressure cuffs predicting heart disease risks. There were also menopause-tracking devices using biological data rather than self-reported symptoms. A smart bed with built-in sensors monitors sleep, heart rate, and movement. It can also adjust positions for comfort, offer aromatherapy, and even contact emergency services if necessary. CES emphasized the importance of digital health tools in improving well-being. Difficult words: prevention (stopping something from happening), insight (deep understanding of something), cortisol (the body’s main stress hormone), progesterone (a female hormone that causes the womb to prepare for pregnancy), saliva (the liquid produced in your mouth to keep it wet and to help to prepare for food to be digested). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Boom Supersonic’s XB-1 made history by becoming the first privately funded airplane to break the sound barrier during a test flight over the Mojave Desert. The flight reached Mach 1.1, 1,360 kph, faster than the speed of sound. Chief Test Pilot Tristan Brandenburg expressed his excitement, saying the plane had never flown better. This milestone is part of Boom Supersonic’s plan to create a commercial supersonic airliner called Overture. The Overture will carry 64-80 passengers and travel across the Atlantic in about 3.5 hours. The company already has 130 orders for the aircraft from major airlines, including American Airlines, United Airlines, and Japan Airlines. Boom Supersonic is constructing a new factory in Greensboro, North Carolina, where they plan to build 66 Overture planes per year. This successful test flight brings them one step closer to reviving supersonic air travel. Difficult words: milestone (important event or achievement), revive (to bring something back to life or use it again). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
